issues.description: Field identifier names in the solution Lecture class do not match the names used elsewhere and the UML in the problem statement. In solution_repository/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java the attributes are declared with snake_case identifiers (lecture_name, number_of_inscribed_students, number_of_guest_students, number_of_lecturers, number_of_tutors) but the constructor, getters, setters and other methods reference camelCase identifiers (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The UML in the problem statement also specifies the camelCase names. This mismatch will cause compilation errors and confuses students about the expected attribute names.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute identifiers consistent. Rename the declared fields in solution/src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java from snake_case to the camelCase names used throughout the class and shown in the UML: lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors. Alternatively (less recommended), update all constructor and method references to the declared snake_case names. Ensure the final names match the UML and the getters/setters so the class compiles and matches the exercise specification.
